From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Platform PM - AcmeHealth <pm-platform@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: VPC maintenance window: conflict resolution & approval path

Hi team —

Following up on our upcoming Private deployment maintenance for AcmeHealth (version bump v2.8.3 -> v2.9.0, kernel + CVE backports). We surfaced a scheduling conflict between your weekly batch job and our default maintenance lanes; wanted to align before we lock an approval path.

Summary / ask:
- Proposed maintenance windows (pick one):
  * Option A: 2026-09-14 02:00–05:00 UTC (3h) — minimal overlap with peak usage
  * Option B: 2026-09-21 00:00–06:00 UTC (6h) — more buffer for canary/validation
- Upgrade scope: runtime libs + quantization kernels; host reboot expected for subset of nodes (rolling).
- Version pinning: we will pin customer fleet to v2.9.0 immediately after successful canary. If canary fails, we will roll back to v2.8.3 (see attached rollback_checklist.md).
- Compliance asks: Neha — can you confirm required log retention snapshot timing for AcmeHealth audit window?
- Action for Acme SRE: confirm preferred window, call out any critical jobs that must be quiesced, and confirm on-call coverage for the day after.

Attachments: maintenance_window_matrix.csv (contains per-rack schedule), rollback_checklist.md, compatibility_summary.pdf

I'll collect responses by EOD 2026-08-07 and then circulate an approval path (who needs to sign off: Acme platform PM, Acme SRE lead, Redwood Ops IC, Redwood Security).

Thanks —
Chloe Martin
Principal PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC maintenance window: conflict resolution & approval path

Chloe —

Thanks for the summary. Our SRE preference is Option A (2026-09-14 02:00–05:00 UTC). That window avoids our overnight ETL aggregate and the weekly billing job. A few notes:
- We need a 30-minute quiesce for the nightly export (starts 01:15 UTC) — if you can guarantee nodes touching the export set are not drained during that 30m window we should be fine.
- We'll provide on-call coverage for the following 48 hours; escalation path will be me (sre-ops@acmehealth.com) -> Platform PM.
- We require that audit log snapshot be taken at least 2 hours before the start time — for rollback traceability.

We will also run a compatibility test against Acme's L4 ingress on 2026-09-07; if you can provide a short-lived canary image and instructions by 2026-08-20 we will run it.

Thanks,
Rajiv Shah
SRE Lead, AcmeHealth
[sre-ops@acmehealth.com]
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, SRE Lead - AcmeHealth <sre-ops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC maintenance window: conflict resolution & approval path

Thanks Rajiv — Option A works for us too. A couple of operational clarifications from engineering:
- Canary plan (we propose runbook step order):
  1) Push canary image to Acme registry (canary tag).
  2) Roll canary to 1 rack (8 GPUs) for 30m traffic soak (traffic routed 5% of baseline).
  3) Run compatibility suite (5 smoke prompts, KV cache integrity check, metric collection).
  4) If green, escalate to 25% of read-only traffic for 60m then continue full roll.
- KV cache: we'll snapshot and preserve the prefix cache prior to canary and will not evict until after full roll.
- Rollback: immediate rollback will be the canary image rollback + re-pin fleet to v2.8.3 using remote override; full data-plane rollback may require cache warmup — estimate 45m to regain pre-upgrade tail latency.

Attached I put a short operations checklist (see rollback_checklist.md). Please flag any objections to the soak volume or timing.

- Dev

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC maintenance window: conflict resolution & approval path

All — quick compatibility and monitoring notes from Platform:
- We validated v2.9.0 against our internal suite (no regressions on top-1 token perf) but there are two known WARNING-level telemetry spikes on Node GC after 20–30min of steady load (non-blocking). We recommend adding a GC-monitoring alert for the first 6 hours post-upgrade.
- Pinning behavior: after canary success we'll apply a soft-pin for 24h (auto-unpin only on explicit approval) to allow observational rollback if needed.
- Config reconciliation: Acme has a custom NLB timeout which may interact with the longer 6h Option B; since we are on Option A, risk is low but please keep an eye on 502s.

I'll add the GC alert to the runbook draft and link it in the shared Drive.

— Rachel
Senior Release Engineer, Redwood Inference

- We'll snapshot the ingestion logs and control-plane audit trail at 2026-09-14T00:00:00Z (2 hours before the start) as requested. Snapshot will be stored in an immutable retention bucket for 30 days (Acme compliance).
- Please confirm who will run the post-upgrade integrity check (I propose Redwood Ops + Acme SRE jointly run the first verification).
- Please also confirm if Acme requires a signed evidence package (we have a template for signed runbooks + checksums if needed).

I will prepare the minimal evidence package template and drop it into the Drive link by EOD 2026-08-13.

— Neha
